examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Rational Function
examples.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{-2}}{2}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}({2}^{-2}-{1}^{-2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{4}-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{4+1}}{4+1}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}-\frac{{1}^{5}}{5} \\  & =\frac{32}{5}-\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{31}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
